answer: In an agent marketplace trading walnut wood, raven illustrations, and quill pens, each agent’s voting power equals the tokens it locks in escrow for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake identities still yields only 100 votes, so creating identities adds no influence. To gain control, an attacker must acquire more tokens and immobilize that capital for the full lock period, bearing its financing cost and price risk.
